rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance: criminal history ban in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about criminal history or run criminal background checks. They also may not say in ads that people with records are excluded, or refuse to rent, end a tenancy, or charge a higher deposit or rent because of criminal history. If a landlord acts against an applicant or tenant because of criminal history, the landlord must give written notice and a chance to respond.
rules.key_value: Criminal history inquiries and use prohibited in rental housing
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, as to current and prospective tenants. Covers advertising, applications, tenant selection, adding family members, deposits and rent amounts.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders. Limited exemptions for public housing and Section 8 properties. Owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as their primary residence. Units under a rental agreement that lets owners move back in under BMC 13.76.130 A.9. Existing tenants subletting or adding or replacing roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation. Civil damages of actual damages or three times one month's rent, plus punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied property of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as primary residence

rules.reason: There was only one candidate, an official city page on the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance. I kept just the testable owner-occupied 1-3 unit exemption and described the other exemptions in text, since they can't be tested.
